The GRACE\u2010FO instrument and flight system performance has improved over GRACE. Better attitude solutions and enhanced pointing performance result in reduced fuel consumption and gravity range rate post\u2010fit residuals. One accelerometer requires additional calibrations due to unexpected measurement noise. The GRACE\u2010FO gravity and mass change fields from June 2018 through December 2019 continue the GRACE record at an equivalent precision and spatiotemporal sampling. During this period, GRACE\u2010FO observed large interannual terrestrial water variations associated with excess rainfall (Central US, Middle East), drought (Europe, Australia), and ice melt (Greenland). These observations are consistent with independent mass change estimates, providing high confidence that no intermission biases exist from GRACE to GRACE\u2010FO, despite the 11\u2010month gap. GRACE\u2010FO has also successfully demonstrated satellite\u2010to\u2010satellite laser ranging interferometry.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1029\/2020gl088306","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2020,5,25]],"date-time":"2020-05-25T00:16:27Z","timestamp":1590365787000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":759,"title":["Extending
